scope: Source-informed authored wooden interiors for five ordinary POTC families; no proprietary game mesh, original interior, or exact historical reconstruction claimed.

sources.title: A Guide to the 1768 Reproduction Schooner Sultana, Sultana Projects/NPS (2003), pp.22–29
sources.source_type: replica operator and NPS original-plan guide
claims: The guide reproduces 21 June 1768 survey overlays of weather and lower decks.
It locates a hand-worked wooden windlass, cargo hatch, scuttles, pumps beside the mainmast, and aft companionway.
The stern cabin had windows, desk and bunk; the central hold had side bunks, with a brick-and-iron galley forward.
sources.limits: Sultana is much smaller and carried swivel guns. This asset retains the game-family dimensions, two-mast rig and twenty carriage guns. Modern head, engine, gas cooker and life floats are excluded; room positions are adapted.

decisions.basis: Central cargo/stores hold with side crew bunks and a clear fore-and-aft passage; a forward brick-protected galley is adapted from the survey-backed replica. This is an adapted, authored spatial decision; cited analogues establish the feature class rather than these coordinates.

Aft window cabin has a chart desk, single bunk and chest, and is entered through a real companionway and doorway. This is an adapted, authored spatial decision; cited analogues establish the feature class rather than these coordinates.

Octagonal horizontal wooden windlass, main cargo hatch, forward scuttle and twin mainmast pumps; a 3m carried boat is optional where final gun and rig clearance allows it. This is an adapted, authored spatial decision; cited analogues establish the feature class rather than these coordinates.

Stern and bow detail remain modest; a removable-pot close-stool is an authored officer facility. No engines, modern flushing head or gas galley are imported. This is an adapted, authored spatial decision; cited analogues establish the feature class rather than these coordinates.
A real open seat frame and removable pot are placed in a measured clear cabin footprint. This is an authored period-furniture adaptation; an inaccessible decorative beakhead seat is not claimed.

A 3m hollow timber boat with adult-scale thwarts, oars and real skids is an optional authored fitting, accepted only where measured final gun/rig geometry leaves a supported bay clear of access. Its compact dimensions and location are authored against measured clear geometry, not copied from a stock mesh or claimed as Batavia dimensions.

The optional three-metre carried tender is omitted on this authored twenty-carriage-gun Schooner: its full supported hull, skids and access clearances do not fit the measured final deck bays between actual gun/rig stations and working hatches. The smaller Sultana survey is an equipment analogue, not evidence that this larger armed game-family deck can retain its exact arrangement.

Selected hold, cabin-sole and forecastle end-bearing stations are inset 0.12 m within the full floor boundaries. This gives separate 140 mm beams and 130 mm knees genuine clearance at adjoining soles and keeps end knees outside the forecastle breakwall. The measured assembly correction is authored; the cited museum/survey source supplies period timber-construction context, not these dimensions or stations.

The retained game-family forecastle rises only 0.28 m. Its authored compact triangular knees bear on the measured main sole, while actual upper beam ends receive shallow fitted notches around the existing main waterways. This preserves both deck surfaces and gives each timber real clearance; the survey source supports hand-worked timber ship construction rather than these specific dimensions.
